description:
FOUND s473t6c (#1501 ROUND 10).

t/op/unlink.t's last two rows are
    $_ = $tmpfile;  my $r = unlink;
    is($r, 1, "retval of unlink with no args");
    ok(!-e $tmpfile, "unlink with no arg unlinked \$_");
`unlink` with no argument is one of perl's `$_`-defaulting list operators, and
PCL's has no default, so it unlinks nothing and returns 0.

This is the named-unary/list-operator `$_`-default family CLAUDE.md rule 11
names: `Pl/PExpr/Config.pm`'s `known_no_of_params` already carries the
"defaults to $_" spec ([1,-2] and friends) for uc/lc/length/..., and `unlink`
needs the LIST form of it (perl: `unlink` with no args is `unlink $_`, not
`unlink @_`).  Check `rmdir`, `stat`, `lstat` and `chdir` in the same pass --
they share the rule -- and add the negative probe (a call WITH arguments must
not gain a $_).
subject: `unlink` with no argument must unlink $_ and return the count (op/unlink.t rows 5-6)
